Basic version (checks the format only):

```regex
^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$
```

Stricter version (month must be 01–12 and day must be 01–31):

```regex
^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])$
```

- `\d{4}`: a four-digit year
- `(0[1-9]|1[0-2])`: month 01–12
- `(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])`: day 01–31

Both match `2026-10-01`. Remove `^` and `$` to find dates inside longer text; you may want `\b` on each side instead.

The stricter version still accepts impossible dates like `2026-02-31`. To reject those, parse the string with a date library after the regex matches, for example `date.fromisoformat()` in Python.
